test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Out of the four organs listed, three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd one.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kidney**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The kidney is part of the urinary system, whereas the liver, stomach, and large intestine are part of the digestive system.
 
• The primary function of the kidney is to filter blood to produce urine, which is different from the digestive functions of the liver, stomach, and large intestine.
 
• Kidneys help in maintaining the body’s fluid and electrolyte balance, which is not a primary function of the liver, stomach, or large intestine.
 
• The liver, stomach, and large intestine are involved in processing food and nutrients, while the kidney is involved in excreting waste products from the blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liver**

 
 
• The liver is a vital organ that performs various functions including detoxification, protein synthesis, and production of biochemicals necessary for digestion.
 
• It produces bile, which is important for digestion of fats.
 
• The liver also stores glucose and helps in regulating blood sugar levels.
 
 
 
• **Stomach**
 
 
• The stomach is a muscular organ located on the left side of the upper abdomen.
 
• It secretes acid and enzymes that digest food.
 
• The stomach muscles contract periodically, churning food to enhance digestion.
 
 
 
• **Large Intestine**
 
 
• The large intestine absorbs water and salts from the material that has not been digested as food, and is responsible for the formation of solid waste (feces).
 
• It includes the cecum, colon, rectum, and anal canal.
 
• It is also involved in the absorption of vitamins produced by gut bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Kidney**
 
 
• Kidneys are bean-shaped organs located on either side of the spine, below the ribs and behind the belly.
 
• They filter blood to produce urine, which is then excreted from the body.
 
• They help in the regulation of electrolytes, maintenance of acid-base balance, and regulation of blood pressure.
 
• The kidneys also produce hormones that are essential for the production of red blood cells and the regulation of calcium metabolism.
